answer: A decentralized network resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to accumulate witnessed work before its voice carries weight. A new account starts at zero, with nothing granted. The protocol treats this unproven state as standing on a small knoll: visible but far from summit. A gale of fabricated identities cannot erode the foundation built by witnessed labor. Established identities stand on a firm mesa from years of checked labor. Because voting weight follows witnessed tenure rather than key count, synthetic accounts stay on the knoll while genuine contributors stand on the mesa.
